scores.Rationale: The proposal leverages mobile sensing combined with passenger/caregiver real-time input to assess real-world driving, which is a meaningful and timely extension of clinic-based evaluation. While this approach is promising and well-aligned with local needs (Long Island) and could change clinical practice, similar naturalistic driving work exists, so novelty is moderate rather than groundbreaking.

Aims are clear and the timeline is plausible given existing pilot work and clinical partnerships; the plan to correlate app-derived measures with standardized assessments is appropriate. However, important methodological details are missing (sample size and power, recruitment targets, specific analytic methods, data security and sensor/processing details, and contingency plans), which limits full confidence in feasibility.

The PI has a strong track record in mobile health and digital phenotyping and the Co-PI is a uniquely qualified certified Driving Rehabilitation Professional for the region, providing excellent clinical and implementation expertise. The team has relevant interdisciplinary collaborations, though explicit roles for data engineering/biostatistics could be clarified.

The project generates pilot data well-suited for foundation and specialty grant applications (AOTF, Mother Cabrini, ASAHP) and aligns with priorities in aging, disability, and digital health. Success will depend on demonstrating reliability and sample adequacy; the investigators articulate reasonable next-step funding targets.

The requested budget is small and focused (single line item for UFOV at $5,000), which could be cost-effective if UFOV is essential, but the budget lacks other necessary items (personnel time, participant incentives, data storage/platform costs, IRB fees) and provides limited justification. The lack of a more comprehensive, itemized budget undermines confidence that funds will support all planned activities.

The application is generally well-written, organized, and makes a coherent case linking background, aims, and impact; the timeline and roles are presented. Some redundancy, minor typographical issues, and gaps in methodological detail reduce clarity in a few sections.
